limitations: Crazyflow errors condition on available valid truth; failed collection parents and missing queries remain visible.

The same-data architecture comparison holds the imported recordings and objective weights fixed. Public-original versus public-excited changes collection support and normalization together; detailed limitations remain in the preceding accepted study.
Development errors select checkpoints and calibrate envelopes; their coverage is not independent calibration evidence.
Parent/bootstrap results concern these conditions and two simulator configurations, not arbitrary systems or application readiness.
Group-weighted geometric ratios differ from pooled physical MSE; all signed response probes remain in raw error summaries.

Both workflows improve on public-original. Neither architecture satisfies its separate frozen preference flag: public-excited is not comparable within five percent, while quadratic-excited exceeds the primary Crazyflow body-rate parent-p95 cap versus public-excited for factual and response errors. These are independent decisions, not an all-case win rule.

Public-excited and quadratic-excited use identical selected input arrays, six base normalizations and numeric loss weights. Equal optimizer-update counts do not imply equal FLOPs or capacity; Crazyflow public-excited selects step zero.

The collection comparison is a practical workflow comparison, not a pure causal intervention ablation: visited states, available prefixes, training-derived normalization and loss scales change together.

Independent numerical reductions cover 250 ms endpoints and tails; all-horizon truth and finiteness are independently checked. Other-horizon numeric metrics, whole-horizon weighted aggregates and bootstrap draws are verified by production replay, not independently reimplemented.
This study promotes no public recipe, controller, update policy or calibrated error envelope, and establishes no arbitrary-system or application-specific adequacy.

result: Public collection and quadratic workflows pass their frozen broad-progress criteria; architecture preference remains an unresolved tradeoff. The public recipe is unchanged.
